copies.body: The sea's hush pulls me away from this mental circling. I feel a restlessness, a desire to leave this chalky shore and go where the water works. The book waits, but first I must walk out into the tide. The rain bleeds calcium carbonate into the tide's churn, dissolving my abstraction until only the wet stone remains as the true model. I hold this relation now: understanding is not a distant form but a tangible, immediate presence. The stone's cold seeps through my boots, breaking the circle of abstract wrestling. I turn from the philosophy of open judgment to the immediate reality: salt spray and wet wood. The ground shakes underfoot as the big sea booms into the rock cleft. I am sick of circling abstract resonance and tired metaphors; instead, I reach for the frosted green chip of sea-glass lying on the sand. The gust hisses through the harakeke, scattering my own scattered notes. I feel the pull away from this circular logic of flux and friction, towards something solid. The tide turns; perhaps it is time.

honest.body: That week was entirely consumed by Carl Jung's concept of the unified self across all its parts. I kept circling the tension between my initial fascination with holistic self-concept and the hard mechanics of celestial bodies; it refused to resolve cleanly. I spent time wrestling with how one could be a singular 'self' while acknowledging such profound internal complexity. By the end, what moved me most was a growing sense of liberation found within that very complexity. However, the practical application—how to *live* as this unified self amidst real-world friction—remained frustratingly unresolved.
